info.name: Sequentia — Public APIs
info.description:
Sequentia's API-key surfaces: the REST API under `/api/v1` and the MCP server.

**Running the whole collection WRITES to the workspace, and nothing here cleans up.** Point it at a workspace you are willing to leave marked, not at production, or run the read-only requests one at a time:

- **Agent API → Feedback** leaves a helpfulness-feedback row against the captured `retrievalId`, which feeds the KB's analytics.
- **Agent API → Report a knowledge gap** leaves a knowledge-gap row in the KB's gap queue, visible to whoever triages it.
- **Ingest (iPaaS) → Create a draft article** leaves a DRAFT article in the KB — unpublished, but real content someone has to delete.

Nothing in this collection deletes any of it — removing a draft, a gap row or a feedback row is an Admin Studio job.

**6 of the requests spend AI credits** on every run: *Agent API → Query (Sequentia synthesises)*, *Agent API → Retrieve (bring your own LLM)*, *Agent API → Verify a claim*, *Ingest (iPaaS) → Create a draft article*, *MCP → query_knowledge_base*, *MCP → verify_claim*. *Knowledge Bases → Query* does NOT, despite the name — it is a lexical article search.

Whether that lands on Sequentia credits or on your own provider key depends on the STAGE, not on the request: **embeddings are Sequentia-billed with no BYOAI path at all** (`ai-gateway.ts`, the pre-call credit gate says so in as many words), and *Agent → Retrieve* embeds the query on every call. Completions do follow a BYOAI key — and where `ENABLE_BYOAI_PLATFORM_FEE` is on, a 20% platform fee still debits Sequentia credits for them. So BYOAI moves part of the bill, never all of it: a workspace can still run out of credits, or collect a 402, on a run whose completions were all external.

**And 1 more carries a flat per-call debit that depends on the deployment**: *MCP → list_knowledge_bases*. It is `MCP_B1_CREDITS_PER_CALL`, which defaults to 0 — so usually free, but not free by contract. Everything else bills nothing.

**Setup.** Import the companion environment, then fill in four values. `baseUrl` — NOT a vanity host: REST is served per DEPLOYMENT, so copy the origin of the direct URL in Admin Studio → MCP Server (e.g. `https://your-cell.example`). `mcpUrl` — the full MCP endpoint from that same page — copy what it shows rather than assuming its shape. It is USUALLY a different host from `baseUrl` (the universal gateway, stable across cell migrations), but a deployment whose config does not know that gateway falls back to this cell's own origin + `/mcp`, and then the two DO share a host. Both ship as unreachable placeholders on purpose — a default that happens to resolve is one a reader can leave in place while their key travels to it as a bearer token. `apiKey` — and NO clickable form mints one key that runs this whole collection, which is the part worth knowing before you start. **Admin Studio → Agent Playground**, with every box ticked, is the best single credential; the form preselects only three of them, and a key accepted straight from it fails most of the Agent API folder. Outside it: `analytics.read`, `articles.write` and `gaps.read`. `gaps.read` is offered by no form at all — that one needs a key minted through `POST /api/v2/api-keys`. The per-form offer lists and which request needs what are in `docs/customer/api/postman/README.md`. And `kbId` — run *Knowledge Bases → List* and copy an id. Those four are all a person fills: `articleId`, `retrievalId` and `mcpSessionId` are captured by the requests that produce them.

The `apiKey` variable is typed `secret`, which MASKS it in the UI and nothing more: a shared or initial value can still leave in an export. Keep the real key as a current value, or in Postman Vault.

**Auth.** Bearer token on every request except *System → Health*.

**Entitlement.** The whole Agent API folder, the MCP folder and *Knowledge Bases → Query* need the agentic API module (Team plan or above). Without it they answer 402 — that is a plan issue, not a bad key.

**Scopes.** Each request names the scope it needs in its own description; read those rather than assuming a universal default. The General APIs form starts with `kb.read`, `kb.search` and `articles.read` ticked, none of which covers the Agent API or the KB query. Only `query`, `retrieve` and `verify` take a broad `rag.query` in place of their dedicated scope; `gap-report` needs `gaps.write`, `index-status` needs `kb.read`, and `feedback` has no alternative at all.

**Machine-readable.** Every request's description ends with a fenced `sq-test` JSON block — scopes, what it persists, whether it spends credits, what it captures and its transport — which is the contract tooling such as `sequentia-test-cli` loads this collection by. The MCP folder is marked `transport: "mcp"`, so a REST consumer skips it while it stays runnable here.

Generated by `scripts/docs/build-postman-collection.mjs` — edit the generator, not this file.

request.description:
Lexical search over the KB's PUBLISHED ARTICLES — ranked article hits, no chunk retrieval and no generated answer. The response names the lane (`lane: "articles-lexical"`) and the pool it searched (`searchedArticles`); when `results` is empty, `noResultsReason` says why: `no_searchable_articles` (the KB has no published articles for this lane — a Document KB looks like this, and so does a PRIVATE article KB whose articles are all audience-scoped; for a Document KB use Agent → Retrieve, which applies the same visibility rules: `kb.read_internal` to see a private KB's chunks, and on a private KB audience-scoped content stays hidden there too — audience labels do not restrict reads on an anonymously public KB), `query_not_searchable` (the lane refuses the query: no positive term, or an unrestricted `OR -term` shape like `data OR -quota`) or `no_match`.

Needs the agentic API module (Team plan or above) on top of the scope — without it this answers 402 while the rest of this folder keeps working.

request.description:
Retrieval AND synthesis, with citations and provenance.

`knowledgeBaseIds` is a LIST — the schema is strict and rejects a singular `knowledgeBaseId`, along with any other unknown key.

`includeGraphContext` only applies when querying a single KB.

No evidence is a 200, not an error: `answer` is `null`, `evidence` is `none` and `message` carries the localised copy. Read "was anything served?" from `sources` / `evidence`, never from `citations`, which also carries graph entities and can be non-empty when nothing was served.

Streaming is NOT available here despite what older docs suggest: there is no `text/event-stream` branch on this route.

**Scope:** `agent.query (or rag.query)`

```sq-test
{"scopes":["agent.query","rag.query"],"persists":null,"spendsCredits":true,"auth":true,"internalRead":true,"captures":["retrievalId"],"transport":"rest"}
```

request.description:
Chunks with provenance and no synthesis — the endpoint for pipelines that generate the answer themselves.

Note `knowledgeBaseId` is SINGULAR here, unlike `/query`.

Two response fields are easy to misread. `relevanceScore` is `null` when the retriever emitted no similarity — that is "unknown", not "irrelevant" — and its range is [-1, 1] (`1 - cosineDistance`, never thresholded), so a legitimate weak hit can be negative. And `provenance` is discriminated by `type`: a Document-KB chunk carries `document` (with page numbers) instead of `article`.

**Scope:** `agent.retrieve (or rag.query)`

item.name: MCP
item.description:
The Model Context Protocol server, over Streamable HTTP. Run these in order: `initialize` returns an `mcp-session-id` response header that the rest of the folder reuses, and the session expires after 30 minutes idle, with 5 concurrent sessions per credential.

**MCP has two rate ceilings, and which one bites depends on the key AND on the verb.** Every POST, GET and DELETE passes a 300 per minute limiter shared **per IP** and applied **before auth**. Only **POST** then checks a second one: `resolveToolRateLimit`/`checkToolRateLimit` are called from the POST handler alone, so the GET and DELETE routes — including this collection's *close the session* step — mount the transport limiter and `mcpAuth()` and nothing else. Throttled cleanup is therefore always the per-IP backstop, never the key's bucket. On POST the key's own `rateLimit`/`rateLimitWindow` applies — and a key minted through Admin Studio carries 1,000 per hour, because the mint route defaults both columns. The 60 per minute figure often quoted as "the default" is the FALLBACK `resolveToolRateLimit` uses only when a key has neither column set — a legacy or programmatically-created credential. So a `429` on the hourly bucket resets on a different clock from one on the per-IP backstop, and several agents behind one egress IP collect the second kind while looking like a bad key setting. These numbers are GENERATED from the constants that set them.

Responses may arrive SSE-framed (`event: message` / `data: {…}`) rather than as plain JSON — that is the transport working, not an error.

Most clients (Claude Desktop, Cursor, LangChain's MCP adapters) speak this for you; the folder is here to debug auth and tool arguments by hand. Admin Studio → MCP Server has copy-paste configs for those clients.

request.description:
Opens the session. The id comes back in the `mcp-session-id` RESPONSE HEADER, not in the body; the test script stores it in `{{mcpSessionId}}`.

**Refuses to send while `{{mcpSessionId}}` is set.** A second handshake would strand the first session — open server-side until its 30 min TTL, with the collection's only handle to it gone — and five of those exhaust the per-credential cap. Run *7. close the session* first; if that session has already expired, clear the variable by hand.

**Scope:** any ONE of `rag.query`, `kb.read`, `agent.verify`, `agent.write_audit` or `agent.execute_action` — the `/mcp` entry gate, checked on every request before the handshake. A key with none of them answers 403 here rather than inside a `200`.


A grounded answer with sources.

`mode` accepts fast / standard / precise. Asking for `precise` over MCP degrades to `standard` — a machine credential has a closed audience scope, which is exactly the case the graph lane declines — and the response says so honestly in `fallbackReason`.

**Scope:** `rag.query` or `kb.read` — any ONE of them is enough. A key without it still completes `initialize`; the refusal arrives here, inside a `200`, as `result.isError`.

```sq-test
{"scopes":["rag.query","kb.read"],"persists":null,"spendsCredits":true,"auth":true,"internalRead":false,"captures":[],"transport":"mcp"}
```

request.description:
Releases the session opened by `initialize`. Answers `204` whether or not the id is still live, so it is safe to re-run.

Sessions otherwise linger for 30 minutes and a credential is capped at 5 concurrent, so skipping this makes the sixth run of this folder fail with `429` — a session-budget problem that reads like an auth one.

Needs no entitlement: closing your own session exercises no paid capability, so this works even on a downgraded workspace.

**Scope:** any ONE of `rag.query`, `kb.read`, `agent.verify`, `agent.write_audit` or `agent.execute_action` — the `/mcp` entry gate, checked on every request before the handshake. A key with none of them answers 403 here rather than inside a `200`.

```sq-test
{"scopes":["rag.query","kb.read","agent.verify","agent.write_audit","agent.execute_action"],"persists":null,"spendsCredits":false,"auth":true,"internalRead":false,"captures":[],"transport":"mcp"}
```

exec: // Cleared ONLY on success. A failed pm.test does not stop this script,
// and this request can be refused before it reaches the handler that
// closes anything — a 401 from mcpAuth, a 429 from the transport
// limiter. The server still holds that session, so wiping the id here
// would leave no way to retry the close and burn a slot of the five
console.log('close refused (' + pm.response.code + ') — session id kept so you can retry');
